title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0561
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0561
Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability in Check Point
Original Issue Date:November  18, 2026
Severity Rating: HIGH
Systems Affected
Check Point Force Firewalls, Check Point Management and Log Servers, Maestro Orchestrator, Check Point Security Gateway, and Check Point Multi-Domain Security Management and Multi-Domain Log Server
Check Point versions R81(EOS), R81.10 (EOS), R81.20, R82, R82.10, and R82.20
Overview
A vulnerability has been reported in Check Point products which could allow an authenticated local user to elevate privileges to root and execute arbitrary code on the targeted system.
Target Audience:
Individuals and organizations using affected Check Point products.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of privilege escalation, unauthorized access, and sensitive data disclosure.
Impact Assessment:
Potential for complete system compromise through unauthorized root-level command execution.
Description
Check Point provides advanced security solutions, including firewalls, network security, endpoint protection, cloud security and management solutions for enterprise environments.
This vulnerability exists in Check Point products due to improper permission assignment for critical resources and missing authorization. A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending unauthorized commands to a world-writable local IPC socket associated with the Gaia OS DynamicCLI process.
Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to elevate privileges and execute arbitrary code with root-level privileges on the targeted system.
Note: This vulnerability (CVE-2026-123039) is being actively exploited in the wild.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned by the vendor:
https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk1000362

title: CERT-In Advisory   CIAD-2026-0061
content:
CERT-In Advisory  
                                                                      CIAD-2026-0061
Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM Products
Original Issue Date: November  18, 2026
Severity Rating: High
Software Affected
Oracle Java SE versions 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, and 27.0.1.0.3
Oracle GraalVM for JDK versions 17.0.21.0.3 and 21.0.13.0.3
Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition version 21.3.20.0.3
Overview
A vulnerability has been reported in Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK and Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition which could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on the targeted system.
Target Audience:
All end-user organizations and individuals using affected versions of Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM products.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of unauthorized access and arbitrary code execution.
Impact Assessment:
Potential impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the system.
Description
Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, and Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition are widely used runtime environments for Java applications.
This vulnerability exists in Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, and Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition Java due to improper input validation. A remote attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending a specially crafted request containing malformed Base64 data to the targeted system.
Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the targeted system.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned by the vendor:
https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html
